title: Check your understanding: Dataset Applications & Leakage Prevention

items.prompt: What is entity contamination data leakage in a clinical predictive model?
choices: A hardware failure in the hospital's power grid
Placing different diagnostic records from the same patient into both the training and test splits, allowing the model to memorize patient-specific traits
Converting continuous blood pressure into categorical buckets
Encrypting medical records using asymmetric RSA keys
items.explain: Entity contamination occurs when records from the same individual appear in both train and test partitions, causing models to memorize individual characteristics rather than general disease biomarkers.

items.prompt: Why is a classification threshold of 0.5 rarely optimal in enterprise customer churn prevention?
choices: Because binary classification models cannot output numbers other than 0 or 1
Because false positives and false negatives carry asymmetric economic costs; retaining high-LTV customers justifies intervening at lower probability cutoffs
Because computer processors cannot calculate floating-point probabilities between 0.4 and 0.6
Because churn prediction requires multi-class softmax loss
items.explain: The optimal decision threshold depends on the financial cost matrix: the cost of a retention offer versus the high lifetime value preserved by preventing a cancellation.

items.prompt: In time-series modeling, why must practitioners use out-of-time temporal partitioning rather than random shuffling?
choices: Random shuffling causes hard drive fragmentation
Random shuffling causes temporal lookahead leakage by using future events to train models predicting past events
Time-series models cannot process shuffled array indices
Temporal splits are only legally required under copyright law
items.explain: Random splitting mixes future and past records, leaking future market or seasonal trends into training features and yielding unrealistically optimistic test metrics.

items.prompt: Empirical Risk Minimization guarantees that a model with zero training error will achieve zero generalization error on unobserved real-world data.
items.explain: Empirical risk minimization optimizes sample loss on observed data. If the dataset has collection bias or covariate shift, empirical risk diverges from true generalization risk.

items.prompt: How does preprocessing leakage occur when standardizing features with mean and standard deviation?
items.rubric: Computing the scaling mean and standard deviation on the entire dataset instead of fitting strictly on the training partition.
items.sample_answer: Preprocessing leakage happens when normalization parameters (mean and standard deviation) are computed across the full dataset rather than being fit strictly on the training split.
